name: Nori Robotics

team.summary: Antonio, founder of Nori Robotics and YC S26 batch, previously did robotics research at Columbia teaching robots through human demonstrations.

product.summary: Nori A3 is a $1,688 bimanual mobile robot featuring 19 degrees of freedom, two 7+1 DOF arms, a telescoping lift, wheeled base, RGB cameras, lidar, and a Raspberry Pi 5, designed for developers and researchers with an open SDK.

market.summary: Robotics developers, researchers, and hobbyists looking for affordable hardware to collect datasets and run experiments.

risks.risk: Hardware reliability and maintenance due to low-cost components like RC-style servos causing jerky motion and precision issues.
Sustainability of a low-cost hardware business model in competition with cheap foreign alternatives.
Customer skepticism regarding real capabilities versus marketing claims for everyday tasks.

founder_depth.why: Founder has direct background in robotics research at Columbia and built seven iterations to achieve the current design.

shipping_evidence.why: They have shipped their first robot, are building the next batch, and provide an open SDK and browser-based simulator.

demand_signal.why: The HN launch received 201 points and 66 comments with strong community engagement and interest in the $1,688 price point.

defensibility.why: Parts of the hardware are open source, 3D print files are provided, and reliance on standard off-the-shelf components limits hardware moat.

analysis.verdict_reason: The team has successfully built and shipped a remarkably low-cost bimanual mobile robot with strong initial developer interest, though long-term unit economics and hardware reliability remain open questions.
would_change_my_mind: Evidence of robust autonomous execution on complex real-world tasks without cherry-picked setups.
Demonstration of sustainable software margins or recurring revenue attach rates.
Quantitative telemetry showing low hardware failure rates in customer hands.
data_gaps: Actual unit manufacturing cost and gross margins at scale.
Detailed metrics on customer retention and active developer usage of the SDK.
GitHub statistics and code contribution activity.
